summary: This page documents the ST_YMIN geospatial function, which returns the minimum latitude (Y coordinate) of all points in a GEOGRAPHY or GEOMETRY expression, returning a REAL value. It notes that the function accounts for the curvature of edges toward the poles. An example creates a table of point and linestring geographies and compares ST_XMIN, ST_XMAX, ST_YMIN and ST_YMAX results across them.
one_line: Reference for the ST_YMIN function, which returns the minimum latitude of a geography or geometry, accounting for pole-ward edge curvature.
key_facts: ST_YMIN returns the minimum latitude (Y coordinate) of all points contained in a geography or geometry object.
The argument must be an expression of type GEOGRAPHY or GEOMETRY.
The function takes into account the curvature of the edges toward the poles.
The example table extreme_point_collection has columns id INTEGER and g GEOGRAPHY.
In the example, POINT(-180 0) has ST_YMIN of 0.
In the example, LINESTRING(-60 30, 60 30) has ST_XMIN of -60 and ST_XMAX of 60.
In the example, LINESTRING(-60 -30, 60 -30) has ST_YMIN of -49.106605351 and ST_YMAX of -30.
In the example, LINESTRING(-60 30, 60 30) has ST_YMIN of 30 and ST_YMAX of 49.106605351.
The example LINESTRING(-179 0, 179 0) has ST_YMIN of approximately -6.883275617e-14 and ST_YMAX of approximately 6.883275617e-14.
The page lists related functions ST_XMIN, ST_XMAX and ST_YMAX in the same example.
